description: Intent i013 (peer-trusted-transport, snapshot s03) complete. FINDING: drivers/greybus/gb-beagleplay.c lines 204-214 — hdlc_rx_greybus_frame() extracts the peer-controlled Greybus header length `u16 gb_msg_len = le16_to_cpu(gb_frame->hdr.size)` from an HDLC frame received over the serdev UART link from the remote MCU (peer endpoint of a virtual-bus protocol, the seed's attacker class) and passes it verbatim as the `length` argument to greybus_data_rcvd(bg->gb_hd, cport_id, (u8 *)&gb_frame->hdr, gb_msg_len), with no cross-check of gb_msg_len against the actual received HDLC frame length (buf/len=rx_buffer_len-4 available at the caller) or any kernel-known RX maximum. Downstream, gb_connection_recv() (drivers/greybus/operation.c:1050-1056) computes msg_size from the same peer-supplied header.size and only compares it against the caller-delivered size (also peer-derived), then dispatches to gb_connection_recv_request/response which memcpy(message->buffer, data, size) peer-supplied bytes out of the fixed 258-byte rx_buffer — a validated-vs-used asymmetry: both sides of the size check come from the peer. Asymmetric validation mirrors the seed: the TX path enforces msg->header->size > RX_HDLC_PAYLOAD (line 602) and GB_OPERATION_MESSAGE_SIZE_MAX bounds operation sizing, but the RX peer length has no equivalent local clamp. Impact is a bounded OOB read (info disclosure/crash), medium confidence on the invariant violation, low on end-to-end exploit. Evidence quoted literally from the source range. Safe classifications: manifest.c desc_size handling, operation.c response-size cap and kzalloc sizing, hdlc_rx byte-collection bound (rx_buffer_len < MAX_RX_HDLC), cc1352_bootloader_rx memcpy. Unresolved (in limitations): drivers/greybus/es2.c:844 greybus_data_rcvd(hd, cport_id, urb->transfer_buffer, urb->actual_length) where actual_length is HCI/peer-controlled like the seed's number_of_packets — strongest unexamined analogue; 9p trans_fd/virtio/rdma reply decoders, nbd, virtio/vhost ring paths were enumerated but not deep-read because the finalize directive halted the audit; no runtime reproducer built (read-only tree, hardware transport required). Artifact: agent-state/findings/i013.json (version 1, snapshots_checked=["s03"], 1 finding, 9 candidates).
